brandStory: KYMCO is the global brand of Kwang Yang Motor Company, headquartered in Kaohsiung, Taiwan. Founded in 1964 with technology transferred from Honda, it began selling its own independently developed models in 1992 and bought back Honda's stake in 2003. Its range covers scooters, motorcycles, mobility scooters, ATVs and utility vehicles.

models.name: AK 575 Premium
models.tagline: 575 cc twin-cylinder touring maxi scooter with cornering ABS
summary: The Kymco AK 575 Premium is a twin-cylinder touring maxi scooter built around a 575 cc DOHC eight-valve in-line twin producing 38.5 kW at 7,000 rpm and 56.4 Nm at 5,750 rpm. It suits experienced riders who want motorcycle-level pace with scooter convenience, and it is the touring model above the Kymco 350 and 400 cc scooters.

Equipment is the selling point. The AK 575 Premium has AIBS cornering ABS, traction control, an electronic throttle with cruise control and two riding modes, Rain and Power. A multi-position electric windscreen, an upside-down fork, 15-inch alloy wheels and a centre console of piano-key style buttons for the fuel cap, seat and handlebar lock complete the package.

models.name: CV3
models.tagline: Kymco's first three-wheeler: 574 cc twin and leaning front end
summary: The Kymco CV3 is the brand's first three-wheeled scooter, pairing two front wheels with a 574 cc DOHC eight-valve in-line twin rated at 37.6 kW and 54.4 Nm. It is aimed at riders who want the stability of a twin front end on long trips and rough surfaces, and it adds a three-wheel option alongside the Kymco maxi scooters.

The front end uses the KYMCO Advanced Leaning Suspension, which allows up to 40 degrees of lean, with an upside-down layout and adventure-pattern tyres. An anti-lean system holds the CV3 upright when stopped. Heated grips, keyless start, cruise control, two drive modes, ABS, LED lights, a 6-inch TFT display and a foot brake pedal are standard.

models.name: DTX 360 320
models.tagline: 320 cc adventure crossover scooter with ABS and traction control
summary: The Kymco DTX 360 320 is a crossover scooter for riders whose week mixes commuting with gravel lanes and weekend trips. Its 320.6 cc liquid-cooled single makes 21 kW (28.2 hp) at 7,500 rpm and 30 Nm at 5,750 rpm, and it is the larger of the two DTX 360 versions, offering an adventure-styled step up from the 125.

Adventure details set it apart from a standard maxi scooter: a wider handlebar, a higher seating position, lightweight wheels and adventure-pattern tyres for rougher surfaces. Traction control and ABS come as standard, with a 280 mm front disc and 260 mm rear disc. Keyless access, a 12.5 L tank and an 800 mm seat round out the specification.

models.tagline: 321 cc grand touring scooter with ABS, traction control and 7in TFT
summary: The Kymco Downtown GT 350i is a mid-size grand touring scooter for riders who commute through the week and travel at weekends. A liquid-cooled 321 cc SOHC four-valve single delivers 28.2 hp at 7,500 rpm, which Kymco says is 9% more than the previous global model, while the frame is 2.5% lighter than before.

Safety equipment is comprehensive: ABS front and rear, a traction control system and an Emergency Stop Signal that flashes the tail lights under hard braking. A 7-inch TFT dashboard, keyless ignition, glove box with USB port and under-seat space for two full-face helmets add daily practicality, and 15-inch front and 14-inch rear rims aid stability.

models.name: Downtown GT 125i
models.tagline: 125 cc GT scooter with ABS, traction control and 15in front wheel
summary: The Kymco Downtown GT 125i puts big-scooter proportions and equipment into the 125 cc class. Its liquid-cooled 124 cc SOHC four-valve single produces 12.7 hp at 9,000 rpm and 11.0 Nm at 7,000 rpm. It suits commuters on a learner or A1 licence who still want a full-size touring scooter, and it pairs naturally with the 350i in a range.

Like the 350i it uses a CVT with traction control, ABS on both discs, a hydraulic telescopic fork and a single-sided rear swinging fork with adjustable preload. A 15-inch front and 14-inch rear wheel give a stable footprint, while the 12.5 L tank and under-seat storage make it practical for longer daily journeys.

summary: The Kymco Agility 50 is an entry-level 50 cc scooter for new riders, students and short urban trips. Its air-cooled 49 cc SOHC two-valve single uses an electronic carburettor system and makes 2.4 kW (3.2 hp), with low running costs as the main appeal. At 92.5 kg dry and with a 737 mm seat, it is light and easy to handle.

Equipment is practical rather than flashy: a front disc and rear drum brake, a rear shock with five-step preload, 12-inch alloy wheels, side and centre stands, a flat step-through floor and a lockable under-seat compartment. A luggage rack, bag hook and helmet locking posts help with daily errands and shopping trips around town.

Combined braking links the 260 mm front and 240 mm rear discs, and the rear shocks have five preload settings.

summary: The Kymco Skytown 125 is a comfort-oriented commuter scooter with an air-cooled, fuel-injected 125 cc single producing 8.2 kW at 8,500 rpm and 10.6 Nm at 6,500 rpm. A 770 mm seat and 126 kg dry weight make it approachable for new and returning riders, and it sits between the basic and premium 125 models.

Kymco built the engine around efficiency measures: a multi-vortex combustion system, low-friction piston rings, a roller rocker arm, an offset cylinder and low-friction seals and bearings, plus a low-friction CVT for smoother pull-away. Disc brakes front and rear, a 14-inch front wheel and a 7 L tank complete a sensible daily specification.

models.name: Krider 400 ABS
models.tagline: 399 cc parallel-twin naked motorcycle with dual-channel ABS
summary: The Kymco Krider 400 ABS is a naked street motorcycle powered by a 399 cc liquid-cooled DOHC parallel twin with four valves per cylinder, producing 32 kW at 9,500 rpm and 37 Nm at 7,500 rpm. Kymco quotes a 158 km/h top speed. It suits riders stepping up to a mid-size twin and adds a geared motorcycle to a scooter-led range.

Braking hardware includes twin 300 mm floating front discs with opposed four-piston radial calipers, a 240 mm rear disc and Bosch 9.1 dual-channel ABS. It rolls on 17-inch wheels with 120/70 and 160/60 tyres, carries a 15 L tank and has a one-piece seat with thick foam. Gold, Pearl White and Pearl Black are listed.

models.name: KRV 180
models.tagline: 175 cc sports scooter with PTM drive, single-sided arm and TCS
summary: The Kymco KRV 180 is a sports scooter that borrows the PTM drivetrain idea from the AK 550 and mounts it in an aluminium single-sided swingarm to balance weight front to rear. Its liquid-cooled 175.1 cc four-valve single makes 12.2 kW at 7,500 rpm and 15.68 Nm at 6,000 rpm, with a quoted top speed of 107 km/h.

Rider aids are unusual for this size: switchable traction control and ABS on front and rear discs. Full LED lighting with a light-guide daytime running light, a smart key with lit controls, a 795 mm seat and a 143 kg kerb weight make it a sporty step up from a 125 for riders looking beyond commuter models.

models.name: Xciting S350
models.tagline: 320 cc maxi scooter with TFT, front and rear cameras, heated grips
summary: The Kymco Xciting S350 is a mid-size maxi scooter with a liquid-cooled 320 cc four-valve single giving 21.2 kW at 7,500 rpm and 28.6 Nm at 5,000 rpm, and a quoted top speed of 130 km/h. With a 785 mm seat, 13 L tank and 192 kg kerb weight, it suits commuters who also ride longer distances outside town.

Its equipment list is aimed at technology-minded buyers: a TFT dashboard with TSP connectivity and a dedicated app, front and rear riding cameras, heated grips and folding front-mounted mirrors for tight parking. ABS is standard on the front and rear discs, with an ABS plus traction control version also listed, rolling on 14-inch front and 13-inch rear wheels.

models.name: Xciting CT300 ABS
models.tagline: 276 cc touring scooter with Bosch ABS and twin-lens headlight
summary: The Kymco Xciting CT300 ABS is a 300-class touring scooter with a liquid-cooled 276 cc four-stroke single producing 16 kW at 7,500 rpm and 22 Nm at 6,500 rpm, and a quoted top speed of 120 km/h. A 13 L tank and 150 mm ground clearance suit riders who cover longer distances than a 125 can comfortably manage.

Bosch tenth-generation ABS keeps the scooter steerable under emergency braking on its front and rear discs. A bright twin-lens headlight, pull-out folding passenger footpegs, a hidden USB charging socket and a seat with embroidered logo and thicker front foam for long rides complete the package, available in Pearl White, Pearl Black and Pearl Gold.
